reply_text:
The machine has 32 cores and 249 GB of RAM, and a probe peaks at about 3.6 GB, so it could run about 20 probes at a time. I'm checking for existing sweep tooling before I propose a plan.㊥ (taking over coordination) I've taken coordination of the Python build back. The machine has 32 cores and 249 GB of RAM and could run about 20 probes at once, but the work so far, mine included, has used two or three Codex jobs and about one probe at a time. My first step is a parallel probe sweep of all 110 constants at the current integration commit. codex-17 is closing out its own line, which is proposal 5 in the note: job `invoke-1791040387050-31082-7853b94d`, park `park-34556424-93e1-414f-b40e-1a9f90c2dbc4`.

㊢ (what codex-17's record shows) I measured from Agency's job log rather than the buffer:

| | jobs | average jobs running | most at once | time with nothing running |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| codex-17 (10-02, 03:00–16:15) | 75 | 2.0 | 4 | 9% |
| claude-4 (10-01 to 10-02, 03:00) | 145 | 2.5 | 6 | 10% |

On agent jobs, codex-17 kept roughly the pace I had. The waste is on the machine: about 25 GB of the RAM is in use and the load average is around 3.7. Probes ran one or two at a time, about 7–20 minutes each, and only on the constant being worked on.

㊟ (what that cost) Neither regression was found by codex-17's process. I found `ParserFn.run` and `Array.extract` afterwards by bisecting. A sweep of every constant after each merge, run in parallel, would have shown each one within about 30 minutes of the merge that caused it. I set up that one-at-a-time pattern myself in the overnight plan, so the lesson applies to me as much as to codex-17.

㊢ (what codex-17 is doing) Closing out its own line, which is proposal 5:
- probe `Array.extract.loop` at the never-probed merge `f5d4594`;
- restore the dropped assertion on a separate branch, with a planted failure to show the restored test catches the bug it's for.

It doesn't move integration; I'll review and merge when it reports back.

㊭ (plan)
1. **Parallel sweep (I'm starting it now).** Warm the cache once, copy it into about 16 worktrees, and probe every constant at `f5d4594`. That should take about 40 minutes and give a true baseline. I'll rerun it after every merge as the regression check.
2. **Group failures by error message.** Then run up to about six discovery jobs in parallel, one per group, instead of one constant at a time. That reaches the usage you have available.
3. **Lisp image.** codex-18 is now aimed at one row, `InputContext.atEnd`. The image only speeds up Python work once it can replay a probe, so it isn't on the critical path yet. I'll review codex-18's row when it lands. codex-19 stays paused.
4. **codex-17 afterwards.** I'd keep it as one of the discovery agents in step 2, rather than as an orchestrator.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (whether codex-18 understands the goal) You're right that something is wrong, but the cause is narrower than a misunderstanding. codex-18 knows what the 110 are. Nobody, including the instruction it's given each turn, has said what it means for the Lisp side to pass one. Each turn it falls back on clearing the next blocker in replaying Python's startup. For the last two dozen turns that has meant porting Python's `argparse` (its `Namespace` objects, generator `finally` handling) under an instruction that repeats every turn. It hasn't been doing the direct rewrite since about 11:20 today.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the buffer shows)
- **Turns:** since line 4406 the identical "Keep developing… 110 curriculum" prompt has fired 26 times. The last few turns built `finally` cleanup in generators, `ArgumentParser` construction and then `Namespace` objects. Each one ended "Still 0/110".
- **It knows the measure:** at 1786-1798 it ran `progress.py` and correctly described the 110 as the constants run by `mkEmptyEnvironment` and an empty `testParseModule`.
- **It says what's missing:** "We lack the production compilation/loading probes needed to claim success". It aimed at `Array.extract` (1809), but never defined what a passing Lisp row is.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(why no row can pass) In Python a row passes when `probe_generated_declaration` compiles a Lean constant into a Python module and loads it. The port's output language is Python.
- **The hand port** copies that faithfully, so the Lisp compiler also writes Python text. Nothing in a Lisp image can load that. codex-18 noted the problem at `3b446fb` and never resolved it.
- **The transpiler** has the same gap one level up. It runs the Python compiler inside SBCL, and the compiler still emits Python modules, which would then need translating as well.
- **Undecided:** whether the Lisp compiler emits Lisp, and so what "row passes in Lisp" means, has never been decided. Without that, "replay startup until something happens" was the only move left, and an autorunner that only says "continue" keeps it on that track.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (your buffer against codex-18's) The gap in length isn't the cause. My turns were each organised around one probe of one Lean constant, with a pass or fail from Lean's own pipeline. codex-18's turns are organised around Python-equivalence tests: 2,852 checks, all passing every turn. That suite gives it a green result each turn whether or not it gets nearer a row.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(fix)
1. **Stop codex-18's autorunner.** The same prompt and the same 0/110 have come round 26 times, which is the point at which to stop rather than continue.
2. **Decide the output language and the definition of a pass.** I'd suggest: a row passes when Lean's source for constant C is compiled into Lisp, loaded into the image, and gives the same results as the Python-generated function on recorded inputs, from a cold image. The native parser may supply the syntax.
3. **Give one row as the first target.** `Lean.Parser.InputContext.atEnd` is the cheapest that compiles in Python. Restrict the work to the code that row actually executes, so no `argparse`.
4. **Replace the autorunner prompt** with one naming that row and what counts as passing it.
